hypotheses: When the agent's reply ends waiting for the owner (a question through the question tool, or a plain question in its reply), a scripted owner (a cheap model given the task's hidden brief and the owner's role, never the code) answers it, and the answer is sent as the next owner message; at most three such exchanges per request, after which the question counts as unanswered in the score and the next scripted request is sent. The scripted owner's answers are logged in the transcript as owner messages.
given the agent asks which board size the game should have, when the turn ends, then the scripted owner answers from the brief (a 3 by 3 board) and the answer is the next owner message
given the agent asks a fourth question on the same request, when the turn ends, then it is not answered, the score counts one unanswered question and the next scripted request is sent
given the agent's reply asks nothing, when the turn ends, then the next scripted request is sent and the scripted owner is not called
given the scripted owner is asked, when it answers, then it sees the brief, the question and the agent's reply, never the scratch repository's code

/plumb:plumb intent I want a very cheap way to stress test plumb. I want Haiku to use plumb and develop a simple playable game. Or feel free to find a relevant benchmark. Actually there could be a rather complex task and one quite simple game. The idea is to be able from one plumb dev command like plumb evaluate simple or plumb evaluate complex to be able to run this benchmark test and see how much haiku or Sonnet is able to implement autonomously using plumb tools. when ever Haiku finds issue, it writes into a file that we can later re-use to improve reliability of plumb

Question: When plumb asks a question during a benchmark run and no owner is there, who should answer it, and should there be a cap on how many questions or turns a run gets?

You said on 2026-10-21: "The idea is to be able from one plumb dev command like plumb evaluate simple or plumb evaluate complex to be able to run this benchmark test and see how much haiku or Sonnet is able to implement autonomously using plumb tools."
Options: No answer, the question is logged as unanswered (Recommended) (The run continues with the next scripted request and the unanswered question is counted in the score. No model plays the owner. Recommended: You asked to see how much Haiku or Sonnet can do on its own, so an unanswered question scored as a gap is closest to that.); A cheap model plays the owner from a hidden brief (A second model answers from a brief you write. Its answers can steer the run, and it may need a cap on exchanges.)
Answer: How can no owner be there exactly? There should always be a question owner in my opinion. A model answers the questions of the other one.

Question: Should a benchmark run have a limit on how many questions the model playing the owner answers, or on how many turns or minutes a run may take? If yes, what limit do you want?

You said on 21 Oct: "There should always be a question owner in my opinion. A model answers the questions of the other one."
Options: Set a limit you name (Recommended) (A run stops answering after the number of questions or turns you give, and the questions beyond it are counted as unanswered. Recommended: You asked for one command to measure how much the model can do on its own, and a run with no limit could run indefinitely. A limit you name keeps the cost bounded without guessing a number for you.); No limit (The model playing the owner answers every question the agent asks, and a run is not cut short by a cap.)
Answer: Both should be possible. If unspecified, questiontool needs to ask the question.
